sources.position: Bedin et al. (2024, Astronomische Nachrichten 345, e20230158; doi:10.1002/asna.20230158; arXiv:2403.08865), Table 1: the barycentre of the pair, ICRS at epoch 2000.0 (162.32821578, -53.31941054 degrees). Luhman 16 A is placed at the barycentre: it really circles it at 0.4535 of the separation (mass ratio 0.8305), up to 1.6 au. Gaia DR3 has only a two-parameter solution for one component (source 5353626573555863424), which Bedin et al. (Appendix B) find unusable. SIMBAD: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Luhman+16
sources.distance: Bedin et al. (2024, Astronomische Nachrichten 345, e20230158; doi:10.1002/asna.20230158; arXiv:2403.08865), Table 1: barycentre parallax 500.993 +0.059/-0.048 mas: 1.996 pc
sources.properMotion: Bedin et al. (2024, Astronomische Nachrichten 345, e20230158; doi:10.1002/asna.20230158; arXiv:2403.08865), Table 1: -2768.511, 358.472 mas/yr (mu_alpha* = mu_alpha cos delta)
sources.radialVelocity: Kniazev et al. (2013, ApJ 770, 124; arXiv:1303.7171), section 3.3: 23.1 +/- 1.1 km/s (A) and 19.5 +/- 1.2 km/s (B) from SALT spectra on 2013 March 12, weighted by Bedin et al.'s masses 35.4 and 29.4 Jupiter masses: 21.47 km/s for the barycentre. Both are uncertain by about 1 km/s and include orbital motion of about 1 km/s.
